original_question: Let (X, g) be a compact Kahler manifold with semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature. Is the fundamental group of X an extension of a finite group by Z^(2m)? After passing to a suitable finite etale cover X* -> X and considering the Albanese map alpha: X* -> Alb(X*), does the fiber F carry a Kahler metric g_F with ntf(F, g_F) = dim F, and is F projective and rationally connected?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Problem 3.6 (cf. [Mat21, Problem 5.2]) in the subsection on semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature; it is posed immediately after Problem 3.5 as the concrete compact-Kähler question suggested by the projective-case structure theorem, Theorem 3.4. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2211.09153))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures essentially all of the content of Problem 3.6: the hypothesis that (X, g) is a compact Kähler manifold with semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature, the question whether π1(X) is an extension of a finite group by ℤ^{⊕2m}, the passage to a finite étale cover X* → X and its Albanese map α : X* → Alb(X*), and the two fiber questions asking for a Kähler metric g_F with ntf(F, g_F) = dim F and asking whether F is projective and rationally connected. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2211.09153))
missing_details: The draft should define the paper’s nonstandard invariant ntf: ntf(M, h) := dim M − inf_{p∈M} dim V_flat,p, where V_flat,p consists of the truly flat tangent vectors v satisfying R_h(v, x, y, z-bar) = 0 for all x, y, z in T_{M,p}. Without this, the question is not fully stand-alone. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2211.09153))

It should make explicit that F denotes a fiber of the Albanese map α : X* → Alb(X*). The paper introduces the Albanese map first and then asks the two fiber questions for that fiber F. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2211.09153))
The rank 2m in ℤ^{⊕2m} should be quantified as 'for some integer m ≥ 0'; the paper does not fix m in advance. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2211.09153))

To stay paper-faithful, the question should preserve the three-part structure of Problem 3.6: first the fundamental-group question, then—after passing to a finite étale cover—the ntf question for a fiber of the Albanese map, and finally the projective/rationally-connected question for that same fiber. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2211.09153))

The nearby context matters: the paper motivates the fiber questions by saying that, apart from rational connectedness of fibers, one can expect for the Albanese map the same kind of conclusion as in Theorem 3.4, and that together with Problem 3.3 one expects projectivity and rational connectedness. A fully faithful stand-alone version should not present these as already proved implications. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2211.09153))
refined_question: Let (X, g) be a compact Kähler manifold with semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature. Is the fundamental group π1(X) an extension of a finite group by ℤ^{⊕2m} for some integer m ≥ 0? Moreover, after passing to a finite étale cover X* → X, let α : X* → Alb(X*) be the Albanese map and let F be a fiber of α. Does F admit a Kähler metric g_F such that ntf(F, g_F) = dim F, where ntf(M, h) := dim M − inf_{p∈M} dim V_flat,p and V_flat,p := {v ∈ T_{M,p} : R_h(v, x, y, z-bar) = 0 for all x, y, z ∈ T_{M,p}}? If so, is F projective and rationally connected? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2211.09153))
justification: The draft is aiming almost verbatim at Problem 3.6, not at a broader neighboring question. The paper first states the projective-case structure theorem in Theorem 3.4, including the finite étale cover, Albanese picture, and the fundamental-group consequence. It then asks in Problem 3.5 whether that theorem extends to compact Kähler manifolds, and immediately summarizes the expected compact-Kähler version in Problem 3.6 by asking exactly the three things reflected in your draft: the structure of π1(X), the existence of a fiber metric with maximal ntf, and whether the Albanese fiber is projective and rationally connected. The only substantive omission in your draft is that ntf is not standard notation and must be defined from the earlier paragraph in the same section. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2211.09153))
